items.before: The first batches of the new insulation lost almost no heat in laboratory tests
items.after: Outdoor trials in a wet climate showed that its performance fell by nearly a third.
why: The second sentence does not follow as a consequence of the first, so a causal transition is wrong.
The outdoor result is a conflicting finding, not an instance of the laboratory result.
The two results point in opposite directions, so an additive transition would misstate the relation.
items.explanation: 'However' marks the contrast between strong laboratory performance and much weaker outdoor performance; the other options claim a cause, an example or an addition that the sentences do not support.

items.before: A 2019 review found that children raised with two languages switched tasks no faster than their peers
items.after: A later study of 1,200 adolescents reported a small but consistent advantage on the same tasks.
why: The later study does not follow from the earlier review, so a result transition is wrong.
The later study is a separate investigation, not an example of the first finding.
The two studies reach different conclusions, so 'Similarly' would hide the disagreement.
items.explanation: 'By contrast' signals that the later study conflicts with the earlier review; the other choices would present the disagreement as a consequence, an example or an agreement.

items.before: Samples of the alloy resisted corrosion for more than a decade in dry air
items.after: The same alloy developed deep pits within months when exposed to salt spray.
why: The salt-spray result is not a consequence of the dry-air result, so 'Thus' is wrong.
The second sentence reports a different outcome rather than restating the first.
The sentences describe opposing outcomes, so an additive transition would be misleading.
items.explanation: 'In contrast' sets the two exposures against each other: the alloy lasted in dry air and failed quickly in salt spray. The other options wrongly suggest cause, restatement or addition.

items.before: The 1985 glacier survey recorded a terminus well below the ridge
items.after: Satellite images from 2020 place the terminus almost two kilometers farther up the valley.
why: 'Nevertheless' would imply an unexpected exception, but the later measurement simply continues the record.
The satellite images are not an example of the 1985 survey; they are a later measurement.
The second sentence adds new information rather than restating the first.
items.explanation: 'Since then' places the satellite measurement after the 1985 survey in time, which is exactly the relation between the two sentences. The other transitions signal contrast, example or restatement.

items.before: The manual claims that the sensor needs no calibration after installation
items.after: The manufacturer's own field notes describe a monthly zero-point check.
why: 'Accordingly' would present the field notes as a consequence of the manual's claim, which they are not.
The field notes are a conflicting document, not an example of the manual's statement.
The two documents disagree, so an additive transition would obscure the conflict.
items.explanation: 'However' highlights the contradiction between the manual's claim and the manufacturer's own instructions. The other choices would wrongly frame the notes as a result, an example or an extra point.

items.before: Street trees lowered afternoon surface temperatures in every block the team measured
items.after: The cooling effect disappeared at night, when the canopy trapped heat near the ground.
why: The nighttime result is not caused by the daytime cooling, so a result transition is wrong.
The nighttime measurement is not an example of afternoon cooling; it is the opposite pattern.
The two findings run in different directions, so 'In the same way' is inaccurate.
items.explanation: 'On the other hand' introduces the opposing nighttime pattern after the daytime benefit. The other options would make the night result a consequence, an example or a parallel finding.

items.before: The harbor's outer wall has survived two thousand years of storms
items.after: The inner basin silted up within three centuries of its construction.
why: The silting does not follow from the wall's survival, so a causal transition is wrong.
The fate of the inner basin is not an illustration of the outer wall's durability.
The two outcomes differ sharply, so 'Likewise' would misrepresent them.
items.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts the durable outer wall with the much shorter life of the inner basin. The other choices would wrongly present the contrast as a cause, an example or a similarity.

items.before: Colonies with young queens produced more honey in the first season
items.after: Those same colonies were far more likely to swarm the following spring.
why: The swarming is a drawback that accompanies the gain, not a consequence of it.
The swarming statistic is not an example of honey production.
The two results are different in kind, so 'Equally' would overstate their similarity.
items.explanation: 'Still' concedes the early advantage while introducing a later drawback. The other options would treat swarming as a result, an example or an equivalent benefit.

items.before: The telescope's mirror was polished to a tolerance of a few nanometers
items.after: Its first images were blurred by a defect in the mounting, not in the glass.
why: The blurred images were caused by the mounting, not by the polishing, so 'As a result' is wrong.
The defect is not an example of precise polishing; it is a separate problem.
The second sentence reports a problem, so adding it as a further benefit misreads it.
items.explanation: 'Even so' concedes that the mirror was made precisely and then reports a failure elsewhere. The other transitions would wrongly link the blurring to the polishing or treat it as an added advantage.

items.before: Membership at the city's science museum rose sharply after the new wing opened
items.after: Donations to its education fund declined over the same period.
why: The decline in donations is not a consequence of rising membership, so 'Consequently' is wrong.
The donation figure is not an example of membership growth.
The two trends move in opposite directions, so 'Similarly' is inaccurate.
items.explanation: 'Nevertheless' contrasts the membership increase with the simultaneous decline in donations. The other choices would present the decline as a result, an example or a parallel trend.

items.before: Participants who napped for twenty minutes recalled more words the next morning
items.after: Their reaction times on a separate task were no better than those of the control group.
why: The lack of improvement in reaction time is not caused by the better recall, so 'Therefore' is wrong.
The reaction-time result is a different measure, not an example of recall.
The second result limits the first, so an additive transition would overstate the benefit.
items.explanation: 'However' marks the limit of the nap's benefit: memory improved while reaction time did not. The other options would wrongly present that limit as a consequence, an example or an additional gain.

items.before: The river restoration removed the concrete banks and replanted native sedges
items.after: Fish counts in the restored reach have barely changed in five years.
why: The unchanged fish counts do not follow from the restoration work, so 'Thus' is wrong.
The fish counts are an outcome, not an example of the replanting.
The second sentence reports a disappointing result, so adding it as another gain misreads it.
items.explanation: 'Yet' signals the gap between the restoration effort and the disappointing fish counts. The other transitions would treat the outcome as a consequence, an example or an extra benefit.

items.before: The coral nursery raised fragments on rope frames suspended above the seabed
items.after: It kept a second set of fragments in cooler water to test heat tolerance.
why: The second activity does not contradict the first, so 'However' is wrong.
The cooler-water set was a deliberate comparison, not a consequence of the frames.
The second set is a separate experiment rather than an example of the rope frames.
items.explanation: 'In addition' adds the second, parallel experiment to the first. The other choices would wrongly frame it as a contrast, a result or an example.

items.before: The typeface was designed for readers with low vision
items.after: Its numerals were drawn to stay distinct at very small sizes.
why: The numeral design does not contradict the overall design goal, so 'Nevertheless' is wrong.
Distinct numerals are part of the design, not a consequence of it.
The two features work together, so 'By contrast' would invent a conflict.
items.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a second feature that supports the same design goal. The other options would wrongly suggest contrast, cause or opposition between the two choices.

items.before: The vineyard's soil sensors report moisture every fifteen minutes
items.after: A weather station on the ridge records wind speed and humidity.
why: The two instruments do not conflict, so 'However' is wrong.
The weather station was installed alongside the sensors, not because of them.
The weather station is a separate instrument, not an example of a soil sensor.
items.explanation: 'In addition' adds the weather station to the list of instruments monitoring the vineyard. The other choices would wrongly imply contrast, causation or exemplification.

items.before: Satellite tags revealed that the birds crossed the desert in a single night
items.after: Ground observers found that the same birds rested for two days before continuing.
why: The resting period is not a consequence of the night crossing, so 'Therefore' is wrong.
The resting observation is not an example of the crossing.
The two findings describe different stages of the journey, not a contradiction.
items.explanation: 'Meanwhile' sets the ground observation alongside the satellite finding as a parallel piece of evidence. The other transitions would wrongly suggest cause, example or concession.

items.before: The kiln was fired in a reducing atmosphere to deepen the glaze
items.after: Each vessel was rotated a quarter turn every hour so that it would not slump.
why: The rotation was a separate precaution, not an effect of the reducing atmosphere.
The two procedures were both part of the firing, so they do not contrast.
The rotation is not an example of a firing atmosphere.
items.explanation: 'At the same time' adds a second procedure carried out during the same firing. The other options would wrongly present it as a result, a contrast or an example.

items.before: The new cycle lanes cut injury rates along the avenue by half
items.after: Secure parking at six transit stations gave riders a place to leave their bikes overnight.
why: The parking does not contradict the safety improvement, so 'However' is wrong.
The parking was a separate investment, not a consequence of the lanes.
The parking is a complementary measure, not an example of a cycle lane.
items.explanation: 'In addition' presents the parking as another measure introduced alongside the lanes. The other choices would wrongly make it a contrast, a result or an illustration.

items.before: The archive digitised its photographic collection at high resolution
items.after: It recorded an oral history interview with every surviving photographer.
why: The interviews do not conflict with the digitisation, so 'However' is wrong.
The interviews were a separate project, not an effect of scanning the photographs.
The interviews are not an example of digitisation; they are a different record.
items.explanation: 'Additionally' adds a second preservation project to the first. The other transitions would wrongly frame the interviews as a contrast, a consequence or an example.

items.before: Thin-film panels can be printed onto flexible backing
items.after: They perform well in diffuse light, which makes them useful on overcast days.
why: The second sentence supports the first rather than contradicting it.
The performance in diffuse light is a property of the panels, not a result of the flexible backing.
The performance claim is not an example of printing on flexible backing.
items.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a second advantage of thin-film panels. The other choices would wrongly present it as a contrast, a consequence or an example.

items.before: The bridge's expansion joints had not been replaced in thirty years
items.after: Engineers closed two lanes for emergency repairs after the first hard freeze.
why: The repairs were a consequence of the worn joints, not a contrast to them.
The lane closures are an outcome, not an example of the joints.
The closures are not an additional benefit, so 'In addition' misreads the relation.
items.explanation: 'As a result' links the overdue maintenance to the emergency closures that followed. The other transitions would wrongly present the outcome as a contrast, an example or an extra point.

items.before: The hatchery lost its water supply when the intake pipe froze
items.after: Staff moved forty thousand juvenile salmon to a backup tank within six hours.
why: The move was a direct response to the lost supply, not a concession to it.
The move was an action taken after the failure, not an example of the failure.
The two events are causally linked, so 'Meanwhile' would hide the connection.
items.explanation: 'Consequently' marks the staff's rapid move as the result of losing the water supply. The other options would wrongly suggest concession, example or mere simultaneity.

items.before: Fewer than one in five respondents had ever used the emergency app
items.after: The county redesigned the interface and advertised it through libraries.
why: The redesign responds to the low use rather than opposing it.
The redesign is a response, not an example of low use.
The two actions are cause and response, not parallel cases.
items.explanation: 'Therefore' presents the redesign as the county's response to low use. The other choices would wrongly frame it as a contrast, an example or a parallel situation.

items.before: The manuscript had been stored in a damp cellar for decades
items.after: Conservators spent four months removing mould from the margins.
why: The mould removal was caused by the damp storage, not a contrast to it.
The conservation work is an outcome, not an example of cellar storage.
The second sentence reports necessary repair, not an added benefit.
items.explanation: 'As a result' connects the damp storage to the months of conservation work. The other transitions would wrongly suggest contrast, exemplification or addition.

items.before: The turbine blades accumulated ice faster than the de-icing system could clear it
items.after: Operators shut the array down during the storm.
why: The shutdown was caused by the icing, not an exception to it.
Shutting down is a response, not an example of ice accumulation.
The shutdown is a consequence, not a parallel case.
items.explanation: 'So' presents the shutdown as the consequence of ice building faster than the system could remove it. The other options would wrongly signal contrast, example or similarity.

items.before: Demand for the clinic's evening appointments doubled in a year
items.after: It hired two more nurses and extended its hours to nine.
why: The new hires answer the demand rather than contrast with it.
The new hires are a response, not an example of demand.
The measures are a reaction to the demand, not a parallel trend.
items.explanation: 'In response' frames the hiring and longer hours as the clinic's answer to rising demand. The other choices would wrongly suggest contrast, example or similarity.

items.before: The seed vault's cooling system failed during a regional power cut
items.after: Staff drilled a second, independent generator the following summer.
why: The new generator was a consequence of the failure, not a contrast to it.
The generator is a response, not an example of the power cut.
The two events are cause and remedy, not equivalent cases.
items.explanation: 'As a result' links the cooling failure to the decision to install an independent generator. The other options would misstate the relation as contrast, example or equivalence.

items.before: The software update removed an outdated security certificate
items.after: Several older devices could no longer connect to the network.
why: The connection failures were caused by the removed certificate, not a concession.
The failures are an outcome, not an example of the update.
The failures are a side effect, not an extra benefit.
items.explanation: 'Consequently' marks the lost connections as the result of removing the certificate. The other transitions would wrongly suggest concession, exemplification or addition.

items.before: Several deep-sea species survive on chemicals rather than sunlight
items.after: Tube worms at hydrothermal vents feed through bacteria that oxidise hydrogen sulfide.
why: The tube worms illustrate the claim rather than contradicting it.
The tube worms are an illustration, not a consequence of the general statement.
The example supports a claim already made, so 'In addition' misses the relation.
items.explanation: 'For example' introduces the tube worms as a specific case of chemical-based survival. The other options would wrongly signal contrast, causation or a separate additional point.

items.before: Early maps of the region placed rivers that later surveys could not find
items.after: A 1740 chart shows a channel running west from the delta that no modern map includes.
why: The 1740 chart is an illustration, not a consequence of the general claim.
The chart supports the claim about early maps rather than opposing it.
The chart is an example of the claim, not a new and separate point.
items.explanation: 'For instance' offers the 1740 chart as a concrete case of a mapped river that later surveys could not find. The other choices would misread it as a result, a contrast or an addition.

items.before: Some plants defend themselves chemically against grazing insects
items.after: Tomato leaves release a compound that slows caterpillar growth when the leaves are damaged.
why: The tomato case supports the general claim rather than contradicting it.
The tomato case is an instance, not a consequence of the general statement.
The tomato case is offered as evidence, not as a parallel separate claim.
items.explanation: 'For example' presents the tomato's chemical response as a specific instance of plant defence. The other transitions would wrongly suggest contrast, cause or similarity.

items.before: The orchestra's archive contains instruments that fell out of use centuries ago
items.after: A curved cornet from 1790 sits in the collection beside a serpent and a lute.
why: The instruments are evidence for the claim, not a consequence of it.
The instruments support the claim rather than conceding anything against it.
The instruments are examples of the claim, not a separate added topic.
items.explanation: 'For instance' introduces the cornet, serpent and lute as examples of obsolete instruments in the archive. The other options would wrongly signal cause, concession or addition.

items.before: Cities have begun to cool public spaces with reflective surfaces
items.after: A pilot project in Los Angeles repainted school roofs and recorded a five-degree drop in playground temperature.
why: The Los Angeles project supports the general claim instead of opposing it.
The project is an illustration, not a result of the general trend.
The project is a specific case, not a parallel separate trend.
items.explanation: 'For example' introduces the Los Angeles pilot as a specific case of cooling with reflective surfaces. The other choices would misstate it as contrast, consequence or a separate parallel.

items.before: The survey found that students rarely used the library's online tutorials
items.after: Only eleven percent of first-year students opened one during their first term.
why: The statistic supports the finding rather than following from it as a separate result.
The statistic confirms the finding instead of opposing it.
The statistic is evidence for the claim, not an additional unrelated point.
items.explanation: 'For example' presents the eleven-percent figure as evidence of the low use. The other transitions would wrongly frame the statistic as a consequence, a contrast or an addition.

items.before: Many desert animals avoid the heat by being active at night
items.after: The kangaroo rat leaves its burrow only after the sand has cooled.
why: The kangaroo rat supports the general claim rather than conceding a point.
The behaviour is an example, not a consequence of the general statement.
The example illustrates the claim instead of adding a new topic.
items.explanation: 'For instance' gives the kangaroo rat as a concrete example of nighttime activity. The other options would wrongly signal concession, causation or addition.

items.before: The coating is expensive to apply and requires a trained crew
items.after: It has already paid for itself in reduced repainting on two bridges.
why: The payback is a counterweight to the cost, not a consequence of it.
The payback is not an example of the coating's expense.
The second sentence offsets the first rather than adding a similar point.
items.explanation: 'Even so' concedes the high cost and then reports the savings that outweigh it. The other choices would wrongly present the payback as a result, an example or another cost.

items.before: The theory explains most of the observed data
items.after: It cannot account for the unusually warm winters of the 1930s.
why: The unexplained winters are a limitation, not a consequence of the theory's success.
The warm winters are a counterexample, not an example of the theory's explanatory power.
The second sentence limits the theory rather than adding support for it.
items.explanation: 'Nevertheless' introduces a limitation that stands against the theory's broad success. The other transitions would wrongly present the exception as a result, an example or additional support.

items.before: The first edition sold fewer than five hundred copies
items.after: It is now regarded as the founding text of the field.
why: The later reputation was not caused by the poor sales.
The later reputation is a reversal, not an example of weak sales.
The two facts point in opposite directions, so 'Similarly' is wrong.
items.explanation: 'Nonetheless' contrasts the book's poor initial sales with its later standing. The other choices would wrongly suggest cause, example or similarity.

items.before: The trail is closed to vehicles and has no cell reception
items.after: It draws more than ten thousand hikers each summer.
why: The popularity is not a consequence of the trail's isolation.
The visitor number is a contrast to the drawbacks, not an example of them.
The second sentence sets a benefit against the drawbacks rather than adding a similar one.
items.explanation: 'Still' concedes the trail's drawbacks and then reports its popularity. The other options would wrongly present the visitors as a result, an example or an additional drawback.

items.before: The new schedule reduced waiting times at the clinic
items.after: Some patients found the earlier appointments easier to reach by bus.
why: The bus complaint is a qualification, not a consequence of shorter waits.
The complaint is a drawback, not an example of reduced waiting.
The complaint qualifies the improvement rather than paralleling it.
items.explanation: 'That said' concedes a drawback after reporting the improvement. The other choices would wrongly suggest cause, exemplification or similarity.

items.before: The archive's catalogue is available online in full
items.after: Most of its photographs can be seen only by visiting in person.
why: The limited access is not a consequence of the online catalogue.
The photographs are not an example of the catalogue; they are a separate restriction.
The second sentence limits the first rather than adding a similar benefit.
items.explanation: 'However' marks the limit on what the online catalogue offers. The other options would wrongly present the restriction as a result, an example or an added convenience.

items.before: The crew pumped the flooded hold dry and replaced the damaged frames
items.after: They applied three coats of primer before the hull was returned to the water.
why: The priming continues the repair sequence rather than contrasting with it.
The priming is a later step, not an example of pumping the hold.
The priming is the next step in the work, not a consequence of the frames.
items.explanation: 'Next' places the priming after the pumping and frame replacement in the repair sequence. The other choices would wrongly signal contrast, example or causation.

items.before: The experimenter recorded the baseline reading for ten minutes
items.after: She introduced the tracer dye and continued sampling every thirty seconds.
why: The dye step is the next action, not a concession to the baseline reading.
The dye step is not an example of a baseline reading.
The dye step follows in time rather than adding a separate point.
items.explanation: 'Then' marks the dye injection as the step that followed the baseline reading. The other transitions would wrongly signal concession, example or addition.

items.before: The first phase mapped the cave's upper passages
items.after: The second phase surveyed the flooded chambers below.
why: The second phase continues the work rather than opposing the first.
The flooded chambers are not an example of the upper passages.
The phases are sequential, not parallel independent cases.
items.explanation: 'Afterward' places the second survey after the first mapping phase. The other choices would wrongly signal contrast, example or a parallel comparison.

items.before: The committee published its draft for public comment in March
items.after: It held six hearings across the county before revising the text.
why: The hearings followed the draft rather than conceding anything against it.
The hearings are a later stage, not an example of the draft.
The hearings continue the process rather than contrasting with it.
items.explanation: 'Subsequently' places the hearings after the draft's publication in the process. The other options would wrongly suggest concession, exemplification or contrast.

items.before: The seedlings were hardened in a shaded frame for two weeks
items.after: They were transplanted into the field once the last frost had passed.
why: Transplanting continues the sequence rather than contrasting with hardening.
Transplanting is the next stage, not an example of hardening.
Transplanting follows in time, not because of the hardening.
items.explanation: 'Later' marks transplanting as the stage that followed hardening. The other choices would wrongly signal contrast, example or cause.

items.before: The tribunal heard closing arguments in the morning
items.after: It issued a written ruling the following week.
why: The ruling followed the arguments rather than contrasting with them.
The ruling is a later step, not an example of the arguments.
The ruling comes next in time, not as an additional separate point.
items.explanation: 'After that' places the written ruling after the closing arguments. The other transitions would wrongly signal contrast, example or addition.

items.before: The drug lowered blood pressure in the trial's first month
items.after: The effect had largely disappeared by the end of the year.
why: The fading effect does not follow from the early success as a consequence.
The later result is not an example of the early reduction.
The second finding undercuts the first, so an additive transition is wrong.
items.explanation: 'However' contrasts the early benefit with its later disappearance. The other choices would wrongly treat the loss of effect as a result, an example or an added benefit.

items.before: The survey asked how often residents visited the park
items.after: It also recorded how they travelled there.
why: The travel question does not contradict the first question.
The travel question was part of the design, not a consequence of the first.
The travel question is a second item, not an example of the first.
items.explanation: 'In addition' adds the travel question to the survey's scope. The other options would wrongly signal contrast, cause or exemplification.

items.before: The ferry's engine failed midway across the strait
items.after: Passengers waited four hours for a relief vessel.
why: The wait was caused by the engine failure, not a contrast to it.
The wait is an outcome, not an example of the failure.
The wait is a consequence, not a parallel case.

items.before: Some fungi form partnerships with the roots of a single tree species

why: The bolete supports the general claim rather than opposing it.
The bolete is an instance, not a consequence of the general statement.
The bolete illustrates the claim instead of adding a new topic.
items.explanation: 'For example' introduces the birch bolete as a specific case of a fungus tied to one tree species. The other choices would wrongly signal contrast, cause or addition.

items.before: The proposal would save the city money over twenty years
items.after: Its upfront cost exceeds the current budget.
why: The high upfront cost resists the savings rather than following from them.
The cost is a drawback, not an example of the savings.
The second sentence offsets the first rather than adding a similar point.
items.explanation: 'Even so' concedes the long-term savings and then sets the immediate cost against them. The other options would wrongly present the cost as a result, an example or another saving.

items.before: Workers removed the old track bed and graded the surface

why: Laying the rails continues the sequence rather than contrasting with it.
Laying the rails is a later stage, not an example of grading.
Laying the rails follows in time, not because of the grading.

items.before: The novel was dismissed by reviewers when it appeared
items.after: It has never gone out of print.
why: The book's lasting availability was not caused by the dismissive reviews.
The long print run is a reversal, not an example of the reviews.
The two facts point in opposite directions, so 'Similarly' is wrong.
items.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts the early dismissal with the novel's enduring availability. The other choices would wrongly suggest cause, example or similarity.

items.before: The orchard's irrigation line was damaged by construction
items.after: The grower lost most of the young trees that summer.
why: The loss was caused by the damaged line, not a contrast to it.
The loss is an outcome, not an example of the damage.
